anchors.name: CCBE guide on generative AI for lawyers
anchors.issuer: Council of Bars and Law Societies of Europe (CCBE)
anchors.binding: Guidance for lawyers from the Council of Bars and Law Societies of Europe.
anchors.asks: Guidance for lawyers on the use of generative AI, published on 2 October 2025 and cited in the CCBE's 2026 technical guide.
anchors.evidence: A test of the tool on your own matters, listing every wrong or made-up citation.

anchors.name: CCBE technical guide on AI tools
anchors.issuer: Council of Bars and Law Societies of Europe (CCBE)
anchors.binding: Guidance for lawyers from the CCBE, Edition 2026.
anchors.asks: Explains hosting options, from on-premises and colocation to cloud infrastructure and vendor SaaS, so lawyers can choose tools that protect client confidentiality. A lawyer must understand the essential functioning of the tools they use.
anchors.evidence: A note of where each AI tool processes your data, quoting the vendor's published statement with its date.

anchors.name: EU AI Act Annex III 8(a): AI for courts
anchors.binding: Law in the EU: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
anchors.asks: AI that helps a judicial authority, or alternative dispute resolution, to research and interpret facts and the law is high-risk from 2 December 2027 (as amended in July 2026). Use by law firms is not in this category.
anchors.evidence: A description of what each AI tool does and who uses it, for your legal team to classify.
